punchline: The writers who look most confident write terrible first drafts on purpose, and the one exception is not well liked.
thirty_sec: Anne Lamott says people imagine writers sitting down confident and inspired, but none of the writers she knows does, and none writes an elegant first draft. She reviewed restaurants: dinners with friends, careful notes, then a first draft that scared her. Her fix is the child's draft, where everything pours out and nobody sees it. A friend names the stages down, up and dental, and the dental one checks every tooth.
